evidence.claim: A CNAS commentary states that the average DoD supply chain spans five to six tiers and that DoD visibility is lost beyond tier two, with prime contractors also generally lacking visibility beyond direct suppliers.

The CNAS commentary argues that defense and dual-use startup capital has largely flowed to would-be tier-one companies while subtier suppliers remain exposed to uneven demand signals and appropriations.
The CNAS commentary says Congress could support vulnerable lower-tier suppliers by attaching requirements that appropriations be passed directly down to suppliers.

A third-party ForcedAlpha casefile identifies defense infrared optics and Western chalcogenide glass as a potential NDAA-driven bottleneck and names LightPath Technologies as one public supplier to verify in later layers.
evidence.source_title: The Optics Cliff — NDAA §834 and the Quiet Rebuild of Defense IR — ForcedAlpha Casefile

evidence.claim: A third-party ForcedAlpha casefile argues that qualified non-Chinese rare-earth magnet capacity may be materially smaller than headline capacity because feedstock origin and defense qualification matter.

memory_update.text: Politics theme should continue to be researched as policy-created demand, regulatory compliance, domestic-content rules, and defense supply-chain chokepoints rather than as a simple election basket.
Defense subtier supply-chain illumination remains the highest-breadth node because DoD and primes may lack visibility below tier two while supply chains can span five to six tiers.
Defense infrared optics and chalcogenide glass is the highest-purity small-cap discovery lane, but it requires primary NDAA, customer, backlog, and capacity verification.
Rare-earth magnets should be evaluated through feedstock origin, qualification status, and defense-specific demand rather than headline mine or magnet capacity alone.
The merged universe is still narrow in lower-tier aerospace components, testing/inspection, certification labs, specialty alloys, castings/forgings, and procurement data vendors.
Later layers must verify each candidate with SEC filings, contract awards, current policy text, customer evidence, capacity data, and market-pricing checks before any ranking survives.

summary: Merged Layer 1 universe frames Politics as policy-created demand, regulatory compliance, defense supply-chain fragility, domestic-content pressure, and procurement chokepoints rather than a headline election basket. The strongest initial lanes are defense subtier supply-chain illumination, cyber/SCRM compliance automation, non-Chinese rare-earth magnet qualification, defense infrared optics/chalcogenide glass, and domestic-content aerospace supplier pressure. The universe intentionally balances obvious reference leaders with underfollowed small/mid-cap or niche second-order names. All candidates remain research priorities only, not buy/sell recommendations.
